What each Livermore department spends, and who pays for it

Pick one of the city's departments to see what it spends, every fund together, and which funds pay for it, each read from the department's own two-block page in the Budget Book.

Choose a department

Who pays for it

Read from the department's Department Funding Sources block, the lower half of its page in the Budget Book (pp.85-125): one row per fund. Each figure is one fund's share of the department, not its whole cost. The General Fund row is the General Fund's share alone; every other row is a fund the city keeps apart from it.

A fund marked internal service is one the city fills by charging its own departments, so the money it pays here was first charged to another department and is counted in that department's cost as well.

FundFund groupAmountShare ◇Page

What it spends, every fund together

Read from the department's Expenditures by Category block, the upper half of the same page: what each of its divisions spends under each object heading, whatever fund pays. Each figure is the whole department's cost under that heading, summed over every division the page prints under the department.

Transfers Out is money moved to another of the city's own funds, not spent on anything. The page prints it inside the division's total, so it is inside this side's sum too.

By division, as printed

DivisionObject headingAmountPage

Every amount links to the extracted text of the page it was read from. A row marked our sum adds the cited rows above it and is ours, not the city's: the page prints a department total of its own, which this site has not read as a figure, so neither sum is presented as the department's total. A share marked ◇ is ours too: one row as a percentage of its side's sum.

What these figures do not say

7 caveats the two documents ship with these figures
  • A fund's constraint tier is our reading of the Description of Funds narrative, not a figure the city printed.
  • These rows are printed once per DEPARTMENT; the divisions drawn elsewhere on this site are a finer tier, and five names belong to both.
  • What a fund pays departments here is not what that fund takes in, and the two are printed by different schedules.
  • The FY2023-24 actual and FY2024-25 revised columns reconcile to each department's own printed total and to nothing citywide.
  • These rows say what a division spends, not what pays for it: the schedule has no fund and no fund group.
  • Each ribbon is a cell of one printed table read along a second axis, not money moving in the direction drawn.
  • Every expenditure ribbon is published as external because these rows name no fund group to classify it by.
